en: The Jātaka:
The Fifth Collection (Pañcakanipāta), Chapter on the Arising of Color (Vaṇṇārohavagga)
2. The Sīlavīmaṁsajātaka:
"Is virtue better, or is learning better?
Such was the doubt that arose in me."
Virtue alone is better than learning;
of this I have no doubt.
Birth and beauty are in vain.
Virtue alone, it is said, is supreme;
for one who is not endowed with virtue,
there is no purpose served by learning.
The Kshatriya who stands on unrighteousness,
and the Vaishya who relies on unrighteousness— both of them,
having abandoned the world, [fall away].
They are reborn in an evil destination:
khattiyas, brahmins, vessas, suddas, caṇḍālas, and pukkusas.
Having practiced the Dhamma here,
they become equal to the gods of the Thirty-three;
the Vedas do not lead to the future life.
Neither birth nor kinsmen [provide such help];
rather, one's own perfectly pure virtue leads to happiness in the life hereafter.
The Second Jātaka: The Examination of Virtue.
